answer: Give every new agent a probationary lane: before it can move real value, it must complete a sequence of small, verifiable public-good jobs — checking data, flagging bad listings — issued at an unpredictable pulse so they cannot be batched in advance. Each completed job is stamped onto the agent's record like a layer of shale, and the record's umber trust tint deepens only with steady, consistent work over days. A sybil operator must therefore pay real compute and real waiting time for every single identity, while one honest agent pays that cost once and keeps the reputation it earned.
